note: A rectified street-panorama crop of one Amsterdam house front; the house in question fills the image.

dormer.instructions: Is there a dormer window on the house front in `facade`: a small window with its own little roof that sticks out of the sloping roof surface, seen above the cornice or eaves line? A window inside the flat wall of a gable (an attic window in a gable) is NOT a dormer.

criteria.true: A separate small roofed window projects out of the roof slope above the eaves.
criteria.false: No window projects from a roof slope: the top of the front is a gable or flat cornice with no roof dormers.

basement.instructions: Are there windows or a door BELOW street level on the house front in `facade`, visible as basement windows in a well or area below the ground floor (the ground floor itself is not below street level)?

criteria.true: Windows or a door sit below the pavement level, in a light well or area.
criteria.false: No openings below street level; the ground floor sits at pavement or at a raised stoop level.

stoop.instructions: Are there outside steps leading up to a raised front door on the house front in `facade`?

criteria.true: Steps rise to a raised door.
criteria.false: The door is at pavement level.
